vjimc-2014-cat1-01.prompt: Find all complex numbers $z$ such that $\left|z^3+2-2i\right|+z\bar z|z|=2\sqrt2$. ($\bar z$ is the conjugate of $z$.)
vjimc-2014-cat1-01.answer: $z=\varrho\,e^{i(\pi/4+2k\pi/3)}$ with $0\le\varrho\le\sqrt2$ and $k\in\{0,1,2\}$: three segments from $0$ to $1+i$, $(1+i)e^{2\pi i/3}$, $(1+i)e^{4\pi i/3}$ (equality case of the triangle inequality: $z^3\in[0,-2+2i]$).

vjimc-2014-cat1-02.prompt: We have a deck of $2n$ cards. Each shuffling changes the order from $a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_n,b_1,b_2,\ldots,b_n$ to $a_1,b_1,a_2,b_2,\ldots,a_n,b_n$. Determine all even numbers $2n$ such that after shuffling the deck $8$ times the original order is restored.
vjimc-2014-cat1-02.answer: $2n\in\{2,4,6,16,18,52,86,256\}$, i.e. exactly when $2n-1\mid 2^8-1=255$ (the shuffle acts on positions $0,\dots,2n-2$ as $k\mapsto2k\bmod(2n-1)$).

vjimc-2014-cat1-03.prompt:
Let $n\ge2$ be an integer and let $x>0$ be a real number. Prove that
$$\left(1-\sqrt{\tanh x}\right)^n+\sqrt{\tanh(nx)}<1 .$$
Recall that $\tanh t=\dfrac{e^{2t}-1}{e^{2t}+1}$.
vjimc-2014-cat1-03.answer: With $g(t)=1-\sqrt{\tanh t}$ prove $g(x)g(y)<g(x+y)$ for $x,y>0$ (via $\tanh(x+y)=\frac{\tanh x+\tanh y}{1+\tanh x\tanh y}$ and an algebraic inequality in $u=\sqrt{\tanh x}$, $v=\sqrt{\tanh y}$), then induct: $g(x)^n<g(nx)$.

vjimc-2014-cat1-04.prompt: Let $P_1,P_2,P_3,P_4$ be the graphs of four quadratic polynomials drawn in the coordinate plane. Suppose that $P_1$ is tangent to $P_2$ at the point $q_2$, $P_2$ is tangent to $P_3$ at the point $q_3$, $P_3$ is tangent to $P_4$ at the point $q_4$, and $P_4$ is tangent to $P_1$ at the point $q_1$. Assume that all the points $q_1,q_2,q_3,q_4$ have distinct $x$-coordinates. Prove that $q_1,q_2,q_3,q_4$ lie on a graph of an at most quadratic polynomial.
vjimc-2014-cat1-04.answer: Tangency means $f_1-f_2=c_2(x-x_2)^2$, etc.; summing gives $\sum c_i(x-x_i)^2\equiv0$, hence $\sum c_i(x_3-x_i)(x_4-x_i)=0$, which is exactly the consistency condition for the curve $y=f_1(x)+k(x-x_1)(x-x_2)$ to pass through $q_3$ and $q_4$.
